about: contio retrieval set (spec §8.2): 24 queries, each with exactly one relevant document among 48; half the documents are same-topic distractors, and queries share few words with their answer. Written for contio.

documents.d01: Sourdough relies on a culture of wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria that ferments the flour, which gives the bread its tangy flavour and open crumb.
documents.d02: A heat pump moves warmth from the outside air or ground into a building using a refrigerant cycle, so it delivers more heat energy than the electricity it consumes.
documents.d03: The Treaty of Westphalia in 1648 ended the Thirty Years' War and established the principle that states are sovereign within their own borders.
documents.d04: Photosynthesis in plant chloroplasts uses light energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose, releasing oxygen as a by-product.
documents.d05: A Rust borrow checker enforces at compile time that a value has either one mutable reference or any number of shared references, preventing data races.
documents.d06: Marathon runners hit 'the wall' when their muscle glycogen stores run out, forcing the body to rely on slower fat metabolism.
documents.d07: Plate tectonics explains earthquakes and mountain ranges as the result of large slabs of the Earth's lithosphere moving and colliding.
documents.d08: Compound interest means interest is earned on previously accumulated interest as well as on the original principal, so savings grow exponentially over time.
documents.d09: The Doppler effect makes an ambulance siren sound higher in pitch as it approaches and lower as it moves away, because the sound waves are compressed and then stretched.
documents.d10: Vaccines train the adaptive immune system by exposing it to a harmless piece or form of a pathogen, so memory cells can respond quickly to a later infection.
documents.d11: In chess, castling lets the king move two squares toward a rook while the rook jumps to the other side, provided neither piece has moved and the king is not in check.
documents.d12: Lithium-ion batteries degrade faster when kept at full charge and high temperatures, so storing them around half charge in a cool place extends their life.
documents.d13: The Mediterranean diet emphasises olive oil, legumes, vegetables, fish and whole grains, and is associated with lower rates of heart disease.
documents.d14: A DNS resolver translates a human-readable domain name into the numeric IP address that computers use to route traffic on the internet.
documents.d15: Impressionist painters such as Monet worked outdoors with quick, visible brush strokes to capture the changing effects of light.
documents.d16: Black holes form when a massive star collapses under its own gravity so densely that not even light can escape beyond the event horizon.
documents.d17: Composting breaks down kitchen scraps and garden waste through microbial decomposition, producing humus that improves soil structure.
documents.d18: The Rosetta Stone carried the same decree in hieroglyphic, Demotic and Greek scripts, which allowed scholars to decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs.
documents.d19: Inflation is a general rise in prices that reduces the purchasing power of money; central banks often raise interest rates to slow it down.
documents.d20: Bees communicate the direction and distance of flowers to their hive mates through a waggle dance performed on the honeycomb.
documents.d21: A suspension bridge hangs its deck from vertical cables attached to main cables that run over tall towers and are anchored at both ends.
documents.d22: Sleep cycles alternate between non-REM and REM stages roughly every 90 minutes, with most vivid dreaming occurring during REM sleep.
documents.d23: Git stores a project's history as a chain of snapshots called commits, and branches are lightweight pointers to particular commits.
documents.d24: Coral reefs bleach when warmer water makes corals expel the symbiotic algae that supply them with food and colour.
documents.d25: Commercial baker's yeast is a single strain of Saccharomyces cerevisiae that makes dough rise quickly and gives bread a mild, neutral flavour.
documents.d26: An air conditioner cools a room by evaporating refrigerant in an indoor coil and dumping the absorbed heat outside through a condenser.
documents.d27: The Treaty of Versailles in 1919 ended the First World War and imposed reparations and territorial losses on Germany.
documents.d28: Cellular respiration in mitochondria breaks glucose down with oxygen to release energy, producing carbon dioxide and water.
documents.d29: Garbage-collected languages like Java free unused memory automatically at runtime, so programmers rarely release objects by hand.
documents.d30: Endurance athletes often suffer muscle cramps late in a race, commonly linked to fatigue and loss of salts through sweat.
documents.d31: Volcanoes erupt when molten rock rises through cracks in the crust and gas pressure forces it to the surface.
documents.d32: Simple interest is calculated only on the original principal, so the amount earned each year stays the same.
documents.d33: Light from distant galaxies is shifted toward red wavelengths because the universe is expanding and the galaxies are moving away.
documents.d34: Antibiotics kill or stop bacteria but have no effect on viruses such as those that cause colds and flu.
documents.d35: A stalemate in chess occurs when the player to move has no legal move and is not in check, and the game ends in a draw.
documents.d36: Solid-state batteries replace the liquid electrolyte with a solid material, promising higher energy density and lower fire risk.
documents.d37: The traditional Japanese diet, rich in rice, fish, soy and vegetables, is often cited when explaining the country's long life expectancy.
documents.d38: DHCP servers automatically hand out IP addresses to devices when they join a local network.
documents.d39: Cubist artists like Picasso broke objects into geometric shapes and showed several viewpoints at once.
documents.d40: Neutron stars are the collapsed cores of massive stars that were not heavy enough to become black holes.
documents.d41: Mulching covers the soil surface with straw or wood chips to keep moisture in and suppress weeds.
documents.d42: The Dead Sea Scrolls are ancient Jewish manuscripts discovered in caves near Qumran in the 1940s.
documents.d43: Deflation is a sustained fall in prices, which can lead consumers to delay purchases and slow the economy.
documents.d44: Ants lay down pheromone trails so that other workers from the colony can follow the path to a food source.
documents.d45: A cantilever bridge is built from beams that project out from piers and are supported only at one end.
documents.d46: Insomnia is persistent difficulty falling or staying asleep, often linked to stress, caffeine or irregular schedules.
documents.d47: Subversion keeps a project's history on a central server as numbered revisions that developers check out.
documents.d48: Ocean acidification happens as seawater absorbs carbon dioxide, making it harder for shellfish to build their shells.
